sentences.text:
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.20 of 2024
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard Sri B.Karthik, learned counsel for the appellant, learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for respondent Nos.1 and 2 and Sri Tarun Ram Aitham, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
Perused the entire material available on record.

2. This appeal, under Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for brevity 'the Act'), is filed challenging the order dated 10.04.2024 passed in L.A.O.P.No.192 of 2021 on the file of the Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad (for short 'the Authority'), whereby the application filed under Section 76 of the Act was disposed of in favour of claimant No.2 therein/respondent No.3 herein.
3.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellant is claimant No.1 and respondent No.3 herein is claimant No.2 before the Authority.
For convenience, hereinafter, the parties are referred to as they are arrayed before the Authority.
2 AKS,J & LNA, J 4.

The undisputed facts of the case are that on a requisition made by the Executive Engineer, M &
MPI, Division No.4, Khammam, land admeasuring Acs.3.14 guntas in Sy.No.684/6 situated at Papakollu Village, Julurupadu Mandal, Bhadradri- Kothagudem District, was acquired for the purpose of excavation of Gravity Canal; that preliminary notification under Section 11(1) of the Act was issued on 26.01.2019; that draft Declaration under Section 19(1) of the Act was published on 11.12.2019; that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting award enquiry, passed an Award dated 21.01.2020, however, compensation for the subject acquired land was not paid as there was a dispute between the appellant and respondent No.3 herein.
Subsequently, the matter was referred to the Authority under Section 76 of the Act and the same was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.192 of 2021.
The Authority after hearing both the parties, disposed of the LAOP in favour of claimant No.2.
Hence, the present appeal filed by claimant No.1.

Alasyam Srinivas Reddy vs Spl. Dy. Collecter, Land Acquisition ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22675892/
1 5.

entities.text: Alasyam Srinivas Reddy vs Spl. Dy. Collecter, Land Acquisition
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before the Authority, on behalf of claimant No.1, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and no documents were marked.
On behalf of claimant No.2, he himself got examined as R.W-1 and Exs.B-1 to B-11 were marked.
3 AKS,J & LNA, J 6.

It is contended by Sri B.Karthik, learned counsel for the appellant-claimant No.1, that the Authority failed to consider the facts that neither claimant No.2 nor his fore fathers were natives of Papakollu Village and claimant No.2 did not produce any document to prove his title over the subject land and as such, the Authority committed an error in holding that claimant No.2 has proved his possession over the acquired land and therefore, he is entitled to compensation.
Learned counsel, therefore, prayed this Court to grant the reliefs sought for in this Appeal.
7. On the other hand, the contentions advanced by learned Government Pleader for Appeals and Sri Tarun Ram Aitham, learned counsel for respondent No.3, are on similar lines.
Both the learned counsels

contended that the Authority has appreciated the entire evidence, both oral and documentary, adduced before it in a proper perspective and came to a proper conclusion that claimant No.2 is entitled for compensation in respect of the acquired land and therefore, the impugned order needs no interference by this Court and the Appeal is liable to be dismissed.

8. In order to claim compensation for the acquired land, Claimant No.1 has to necessarily prove that he is the owner thereof 4 AKS,J & LNA, J and at his instance, the Reference has been made under Section 76 of the Act.
9.

It is the case of the claimant No.1 that he purchased the acquired land under sada sale deed dated 09.06.2005 from Mudigonda Mysaiah, who purchased the said property from original assignee by name Srikonda Laxmi; that since the date of purchase, claimant No.1 has been in possession and enjoyment of the acquired land; and that claimant No.2 is a non-tribe and not resident of Papakollu Village and as such, he is not entitled to any compensation.
10.

Claimant No.1 except examining himself as P.W-1 and his vendor as P.W-2 failed to produce any documentary evidence including the alleged sada sale deed dated 09.06.2005 to prove his title or possession over the acquired land.
In other words, claimant No.1 has failed to substantiate his case that he is the owner of the acquired land by way of producing any document before the Authority.

11. That apart, P.W-1 in his cross-examination deposed as under:-
"It is true that subject matter of the property is situated in the agency area and prohibited under Regulation-1 5 AKS,J & LNA, J of 1970.
I am not a schedule Tribe.
I do not know about the prohibition in Regulation 1 of 1970."

12. From the above categorical statement of P.W-1, it is clear that the acquired land falls in Scheduled Agency Area and therefore, the same is protected under Regulation 1 of 1970, which bans all land transactions between tribals and non-tribals as well as non-tribals and non-tribals.

The Alasyam Srinivas Reddy vs Spl. Dy. Collecter, Land Acquisition ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22675892/
2

entities.text: Alasyam Srinivas Reddy vs Spl. Dy. Collecter, Land Acquisition
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: acquired land is recorded as 'poramboke' in the revenue records and admittedly, claimant No.1 is not a tribal.

Therefore, transactions, if any, entered by claimant No.1 with his vendor with respect to the acquired land, have no sanctity in law and the transactions are void and as such, he has no right or title over the said land.

13. On the other hand, perusal of record discloses that claimant No.2 has filed Ex.B-1-Community and Birth Certificate issued by Tahsildar, which shows that he belongs to Schedule Tribe- Naikod-6 and Ex.B-10-Residence Certificate issued by Tahsildar.
Thus, Exs.B-1 and B-10-certificates falsifies the case of claimant No.1 that claimant No.2 is a non-tribal and non-resident of Papakollu Village.
14. Claimant No.2 got marked Ex.B-5-Pahani and Ex.B-11-Sisth receipt issued in respect of acquired land.
6 AKS,J & LNA, J 15.

Here, it is appropriate to refer to the definition of "land owner" under Section 3(r) of the Act,
which is reproduced hereunder for better appreciation:-

"Land owner" includes any person,--
(i) whose name is recorded as the owner of the land or building or part thereof, in the records of the authority concerned; or (ii) any person who is granted forest rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007) or under any other law for the time being in force; or (iii)who is entitled to be granted Patta rights on the land under any law of the State including assigned lands; or (iv) any person who has been declared as such by an order of the court or Authority."
16.

entities.text: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In the light of the above definition coupled with Exs.B-5 and B-11, it is clear that claimant No.2 is able to prove that he is in possession of the acquired land.

17. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the opinion that claimant No.1 has miserably failed to prove his title or right over the acquired land, thereby, disentitling him to get compensation for the acquired land.

18. Therefore, taking into account the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered view that the 7 AKS,J & LNA, J Authority has not committed any irregularity or infirmity in passing the impugned order and as such, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed.
19.
Accordingly, the Appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
